title: Principal registry is pluggable and returns only a boolean
asA: operator running anything from a solo-operator deployment to a multi-tenant tree
iWant: the auth flow to ask exactly one question of my registry (is this address registered) and receive only a boolean
soThat: principal shape (single email, allow-list, database query) is my decision and not the blueprint's

acceptanceCriteria.description: The magic-link routes call the principal-registry through a single isRegistered(email) method returning a Promise resolving to a boolean; no other registry method is called on the auth path.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the auth code path is walked from POST /login through registration lookup
acceptanceCriteria.when: the outgoing calls to the registry interface are enumerated
acceptanceCriteria.then: only isRegistered is invoked, with only the submitted email string, and only the resolved boolean is consumed

acceptanceCriteria.description: A registry that returns false for a submission produces an identical POST /login response to a registry that returns true; the registry answer is invisible in the response body, status, and Content-Type.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same email string is submitted twice, once against a registry that returns false and once against a registry that returns true
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response bodies are byte-identical, the statuses are equal, and the Content-Type headers are equal

acceptanceCriteria.description: The blueprint ships a single-address registry implementation for solo-operator deployments; the implementation reads one email from configuration and returns true for that email and false for every other input.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the single-address registry is instantiated with a configured email
acceptanceCriteria.when: isRegistered is called with the configured email, a different email, an empty string, and a malformed value in turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the resolved boolean is true only for the configured email and false for every other case
